notes: Written to ui-demos/repair-log-v3/SPEC.json per the coordinator's redirect (pipeline/proposals/ux-agent.json and pipeline/BRIEF.md were both lost to concurrent overwrites; this file is the durable source for this cycle, mirroring how ui-demos/repair-log-v3/BRIEF.md already relocated the brief for the same reason). This spec describes the ALREADY-BUILT ui-demos/repair-log-v3/index.html rather than re-deriving a competing design: I audited the live file (CSS, the four SCENARIOS objects, and the load/interaction script) line by line against RULINGS.md and against the game source (customers.ts, kit.ts, patch-cells.ts, run-reducer.ts, content/arc.ts) rather than trusting the file's own header comment. I agree with both calls the coordinator made ahead of me (THE BILL over the verdict as focal, matching my own independent conclusion from the same run-reducer.ts fact before I was interrupted; and run.strain<=35 as the sole --r-warn owner, also matching my own conclusion). Five things I found while auditing are flagged in this item's own `flaggedConcerns` field rather than silently fixed, since I do not touch ui-demos/ directly: a computed type-scale ratio shortfall against law 2's 2.2x benchmark (shown with the arithmetic), a factual mismatch in the STRAINED scenario's tier/day math against Bram Hollander's real customer data, an unhandled 'no piece this ticket' branch, a duplicate sfxr preset that should collapse into the pending loadout-eva instrumentLock item, and a minor role-token comment overclaim. None of these are loremaster- or tutorial-gate-shaped (this cycle is pure UI per RULINGS Process and the brief), so none became an order; they are implementation and craft notes for the Orchestrator's next pass on this file. Zero new sfx items are proposed: every sound this surface's motion needs already exists in the shipped palette (unlock, press, granted, tick) or is covered by the loadout-eva cycle's still-pending instrumentLock item, which this surface should reuse rather than fork under the demo-local name 'ledgerLock'.

items.status: describes the built demo at ui-demos/repair-log-v3/index.html; see flaggedConcerns for what I think should change before sign-off
items.spec:
REPAIR.LOG rebuilt as a KP/OS v3 instrument panel at ui-demos/repair-log-v3/index.html, standalone (links ../_shared/kp.css + ../_shared/system.css + the Silkscreen/VT323/IBM-Plex-Mono stack, vanilla JS, no framework), following the loadout-eva build recipe verbatim: the role-token block, the six-layer FLAT/OFF glass, the real-resolution scaled stage rig, and the typeIn/countUpNode/later choreography helpers are ported class-for-class from ui-demos/loadout-eva/index.html rather than re-derived. Window chrome keeps the .term/.term-bar/.term-body naming, 3px var(--r-hazard) border (loadout used --r-hazard for the same edge), the 9px/26px drop-shadow, solid-ink title bar reading REPAIR.LOG.

GLANCE-ORDER ARGUMENT (the one design call this page makes on its own account, per its own header comment, lines 19-29): RULINGS.md's panel queue note ('the verdict is the obvious focal element') is OVERRULED. run-reducer.ts's `duelFinished` case routes a loss to screen 'runEnd' with lastResult null, and the finale win to 'finaleWin' (kernel-panic-site/app/src/game/run-reducer.ts, the block setting `lastResult: { won: true, ... }` under the ordinary win path, lines ~416-417 of report.tsx's own import chain confirm `lastResult.won` is never false in practice). REPAIR.LOG therefore only ever renders on a win, so the literal string 'REPAIR LOGGED' is INVARIANT on this surface and carries zero information ticket to ticket. A constant cannot be a defensible focal element under law 2 ('one focal element... the largest element' must be the thing worth looking at first). What varies is the transaction: what the ticket credited and what it billed in strain. So THE BILL, not the verdict, is focal, and the verdict is demoted to masthead-slab scale. I agree with this reasoning; it is the same conclusion I had independently reached from the same source fact before this rewrite request arrived, and I would have made the identical call.

glanceOrder.1st_focal: THE BILL (grid-area `bill`, zone Z3): a three-cell row, `.rl-cell` x3 inside `.rl-bill`, built by `buildBill()`. Cell 1 `// CREDITED` (the ticket's credited total, `.rl-num`, unit `CR`, itemized `payRows` receipt below). Cell 2 `// BILLED` (this ticket's strain cost, `.rl-num`, unit `STRAIN` or blank when clean, itemized `chipRows` receipt, the strain-left meter and 'STRAIN LEFT' foot readout, and the ONLY owner of --r-warn on the page). Cell 3 `// [piece head]` (what the ticket recovered: a `PatchGlyph` at 46px standing in for a third numeral, noun, status pill, typed flavour line). All three share `.rl-bracket` heavy hazard corner brackets, scoped to exactly these three cells and nowhere else on the page, per law 4. This mirrors LOADOUT.CFG's own precedent of a MULTI-numeral focal GROUP (the SCAN/ATTACK/DEFEND trinity, three hero numerals named collectively as loadout-eva's '1st'), not a single number; I read this as the correct application of the same idiom, not a deviation from it.
glanceOrder.2nd: THE CACHE (grid-area `cache`, zone Z5): the AUGMENT CACHE draft, `.rl-div` hazard-stripe header with a live PICK ONE / INSTALLED / DRY state tag, then either 3 `.rl-card` draft cards, the `.rl-dry` message, or the `.rl-swap` EJECT panel. Ranked 2nd because it is the one thing on the surface the player must act on; the built page's own rig caption states this explicitly ('the AUGMENT CACHE, which is the only thing here that needs a hand').
glanceOrder.3rd: THE MASTHEAD (grid-area `mast`, zone Z1): the verdict slab 'REPAIR LOGGED' at `--rl-fs-slab` (clamp(22px, 3.4cqi, 32px)), always nominal (`--r-ok`), plus the client's typed win-line quote (`.rl-quote`, the one line of human voice on an instrumentation page) and the CLIENT/DEVICE chips. Present and legible, never extreme scale, because it is confirmatory chrome for an outcome that is never in doubt on this screen.
glanceOrder.4th: THE TRACE (grid-area `trace`, zone Z4): the ECG strain trace (`.rl-scope`, the surface's signature readout, one clean SVG grid + polyline + hazard trap-round tick marks) with the dive log (`.rl-log`, 2 columns, capped at 8 lines) sitting directly under the trace it annotates, both at support/body scale.
glanceOrder.ambient: the CLIENT CAM (grid-area `gutter`, zone Z2's `.rl-cam`, the diegetic shop-camera photo, `--r-aux`) and the four telemetry ticks plus the PATCH POUCH strip that share the gutter column with it. Deliberately never competing: the gutter never gets a container of its own scale ramp beyond the tick/label floors.

roleTokens.r-struct: the CLIENT CAM bezel border only (`.rl-cam{border:2px solid var(--r-struct);}`). General panel hairlines (`.rl-cell`, `.rl-scope`, `.rl-foot`) use the pre-existing `--ch-faint`/`--ch-dim` derived tones instead, which still recolour per scheme because `--ch` itself is redefined by `data-scheme`. This is not an inconsistency: it matches loadout-eva's own identically narrow application of `--r-struct` to `.lo-mon`'s bezel alone, with `.lo-panel` also on `--ch-faint`.
roleTokens.r-note: naming-only annotation: the masthead eyebrow, the CR/STRAIN unit captions, the four gutter tick labels, the 'CLIENT CAM' spine, the patch-piece noun (STRAIGHT/ELBOW/TEE/CROSS), the draft-card kind tags (BOOST/CONFIG), and the 'STRAIN LEFT' foot label until the alarm overrides it. It does NOT reach the bill cells' own `// CREDITED` / `// BILLED` / `// [piece head]` name labels (`.rl-cname{color:var(--ch);}`, plain base ink) -- that matches loadout-eva's `.lo-pname{color:var(--ch);}` precedent (a panel's own identifying name is chrome-weight, not annotation-weight), but it means the file's own header-comment line 39 ('note owns... the // prefixes') overclaims slightly against its own CSS. Harmless (the CSS is right, matching the reference build); worth tightening the comment's wording, not the rule.
roleTokens.r-line: live data: the ECG polyline stroke, every receipt row's numeric value (`.rl-receipt li em{color:var(--r-line);}`), the strain-left meter's lit segments outside the alarm band, the pouch-glyph arms via the shared `.kp-pp-arm` vocabulary, and the footer battery pips.
roleTokens.r-data: the two BILL hero numerals (CREDITED, BILLED) and nothing else (`.rl-num{color:var(--r-data);}`), overridden to `--r-ok` on the BILLED cell's CLEAN word-state and to `--r-warn` in the risk band. This widens RULINGS' original 'the focal numeral' (singular) to 'the two hero numerals' of the compound bill row, matching the pivot to a paired focal group; I agree with this reading rather than flagging it.
roleTokens.r-ok: NOMINAL: the verdict slab (always, since a loss never reaches this screen), the BILLED cell's CLEAN state, the picked draft card's border + reticle corner-ticks (`.rl-card.picked`) + its `.rl-stamp` INSTALLED badge, the fresh pouch slot, the RECOVERED piece's uncapped BANKED status pill, the strain-left meter's nominal band (>70), and the AUGMENT CACHE header's live 'PICK ONE' state tag specifically -- the SAME tag dims to `--ch-dim` once resolved to INSTALLED or DRY (`state.className = picked ? 'done' : ''`), so r-ok here marks 'this decision is open and awaiting you', the same 'live/ready' reading loadout-eva's own `.lo-slab.is-ready` used, not 'you already succeeded'.
roleTokens.r-warn: risk, exactly one owner: the BILLED cell's strain-LEFT reading, armed at `run.strain <= 35` (`RISK_BAND = 35`, the identical band LOADOUT.CFG uses, so the number means one thing across the desktop). Channels beyond colour: inverse video (`.rl-cell.is-risk .rl-num{background:var(--r-warn);color:var(--px-void);}`), a composited difference-blend blink on a promoted layer (`.rl-riskflash`, `rl-risk-blink 1.2s steps(2) infinite`, matching the exact idiom and cadence loadout-eva measured at 9.3ms p95), and the strain-left meter's own segment count as a position signal that survives a colourblind reader with the colour channel removed entirely. That is four channels total against the law's minimum of two. Nothing else on the surface ever takes it: the capped-bill receipt row, the LEFT ON THE BENCH status, trap markers on the trace, and the lost pouch slot all take --r-hazard instead, confirmed in the CSS, not just asserted in the header comment.
roleTokens.r-aux: the CLIENT CAM's own imagery: the ink-tint overlay (`.rl-cam .tint`, multiply-blended onto the 1-bit dither) and the bottom `.rl-camtag` caption pill (e.g. 'ON THE GOOD LIST', 'TILL RESTORED'). The top-left REC pip stays `--r-hazard` (matching loadout-eva's own REC treatment): a deliberate split between 'this is the imagery's own signal class' (aux) and 'this is generic recording-light chrome, identical on every camera in the OS' (hazard).
roleTokens.r-hazard: structural red: the window's own 3px edge, the heavy corner brackets on exactly the three THE BILL cells (all three, correctly, since together they ARE the one focal group -- not a partial/inconsistent application), the AUGMENT CACHE zone-boundary stripe (`.rl-div i`), the CLIENT CAM's REC pip, hazard tick marks on the ECG trace at every trap round (`.rl-scope line.trap`), the capped-bill inverse receipt row, the LEFT ON THE BENCH piece-status pill, and the lost pouch slot's dashed border and glyph tint.

fluid.containers: `.rl-wrap` (wraps `.rl-grid`, `container-type:inline-size;container-name:rl;`) drives the one binary breakpoint at 700px per law 3. Each `.rl-cell` (all three bill cells) additionally sets its own `container-type:inline-size`, so `.rl-num`'s cqi resolves against ITS OWN cell width, not the window's, matching loadout-eva's `.lo-panel` precedent exactly.
fluid.typeRamp: all defined once on `.rl-grid` and consumed everywhere below it (cqi in a custom property resolves at the use site, per RULINGS' documented gotcha, so a receipt row inside a `.rl-cell` container lands at a different absolute size than the masthead quote even though both reference `--rl-fs-body`): `--rl-fs-body: clamp(19px, calc(1cqi + 17px), 21px)` (VT323 floor, exact), `--rl-fs-label: clamp(9px, calc(0.6cqi + 8px), 11px)` (Silkscreen floor, exact), `--rl-fs-pill: clamp(9px, calc(0.5cqi + 8.5px), 10.5px)`, `--rl-fs-slab: clamp(22px, 3.4cqi, 32px)`, `--rl-fs-tickl: clamp(8px, calc(0.4cqi + 7.5px), 9px)`, `--rl-fs-tickv: clamp(12px, calc(0.8cqi + 10px), 14px)`, `--rl-fs-log: clamp(15px, calc(0.7cqi + 13px), 17px)` (receipt rows, dive-log lines, and the piece flavour line all share this one). The bill hero numeral is `clamp(44px, 26cqi, 78px)` inside its own `.rl-cell` container; the CLEAN word-state swaps to the smaller `clamp(30px, 17cqi, 52px)`.
fluid.breakpoint: `@container rl (min-width: 700px)` is the WIDE tier: `.rl-grid{grid-template-columns:190px 1fr; grid-template-areas:"mast mast" "gutter bill" "gutter trace" "cache cache" "foot foot";}`, the gutter beside bill+trace (never its own row: a 234px camera cell next to two short zones is free height, matching the 'a row you do not share is a row you pay for in full' lesson), `.rl-bill{grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr 1.15fr;}` (the piece cell runs slightly wider than the two numeral cells), `.rl-log{grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr;}`, `.rl-draft{grid-template-columns:repeat(3,1fr);}`. A second, tighter rule at `@container rl (min-width:700px) and (max-width:800px)` (the 790px laptop window's ~760px content box) narrows the gutter to 176px, crops the CLIENT CAM to 162x186 (a CROP of the same 1:1 print, never a downscale, per law 5), and tightens cell/card padding. Below 700px (a tiling fallback only; none of the three supported viewports reach it) `.rl-grid[data-tab]` pages between a THE TICKET tab (bill+cache) and a THE DIVE tab (gutter+trace) behind `.rl-tabs`, with the masthead persistent above both.
fluid.measuredViewports: 16:9 term width 900px, 21:9 980px, laptop 1280x800 term width 790px; all three resolve `VP.win - 32 >= 700` in the rig's own `measure()` function, i.e. all three land WIDE and render the identical arrangement, satisfying law 3's supported-viewport requirement.

cuts.item: the four boxed telemetry sparklines (RAM FLOW, ROTATIONS, TRAP FEED, LINK NOISE)
cuts.why: the shipped SVGs were synthetic decorative noise (a seeded random walk, not real per-turn telemetry) duplicating numbers already legible elsewhere; four boxes of the same idea could not survive being shrunk to fit the ceiling without dissolving into noise. Their VALUES survive as four unboxed `.rl-tick` rows at the gutter's own lowest priority (RAM FLOW, OVER PAR, TRAPS SPRUNG, LINK NOISE), which is the honest weight for numbers nobody needs to act on.

cuts.item: the patch-piece poster's separate title/paragraph/status card
cuts.action: folded into THE BILL's third cell rather than kept as a fourth freestanding block
cuts.why: a dropped patch piece is a line item on the ticket's receipt, the same rank as what it credited and what it billed, so it becomes the bill's third cell at the same weight as the two numerals (the PatchGlyph doing the work a numeral does in the other two), instead of a separate lower-priority card competing for its own row.

cuts.item: the DIVE LOG rail, 14 lines single column
cuts.action: capped at 8 lines (`S.log.slice(0,8)`), reflowed to 2 columns under the trace it annotates
cuts.why: the historical depth of the bus log is the least decision-relevant content on the page; halving it and running it in 2 columns keeps the data (the log is not removed) while paying far less height for it, and physically pairs it with the ECG trace it is glossing.

cuts.action: replaces the 3 draft cards IN PLACE inside `#cachebody` rather than opening as an added row beneath them
cuts.why: a bays-full pick is still one decision with one footprint; giving it a second row would grow the window exactly on the scenario that is already fullest (bays full implies a longer kit list and, per the STRAINED scenario, an armed alarm at the same time).

items.cutsNote: law 8 step 3 (always-visible descriptions demoted to hover/focus/tap popups) is not exercised here and I think correctly so: THE CACHE never shows more than 3 card descriptions at once (2 boosts/configs plus, in the EJECT case, up to `S.kit.length` eject targets, capped at 4 in the built STRAINED scenario), well under LOADOUT.CFG's 5-persistent-description problem that step 3 was written for.

loadChoreography.reducedMotionRule: every stage below collapses to its settled state in one synchronous frame under prefers-reduced-motion (`later()` calls its callback immediately rather than deferring, `countUpNode`/`typeIn` write the final value directly, the ECG polyline never receives a stroke-dashoffset at all so it renders fully drawn); sound is not gated by reduced motion and still fires at the same relative points, per the established dadlog/loadout-eva precedent.
timeline: t=60ms: the CLIENT CAM's ink shade wipes up, `rl-wipe 640ms steps(13)`
t=200ms: the ECG trace draws itself in on a stroke-dash sweep, `620ms steps(14)`
t=240ms: the client's win-line quote begins typing (`typeIn`, ~12ms/char)
t=300ms: THE BILL's CREDITED numeral begins its count-up (34ms/step); its `ledgerLock` settle-voice fires once the count completes, at t=300+22*34=1048ms
t=300ms + i*90ms: the dive-log lines type in, one `typeIn` call per line, staggered 90ms apart
t=360ms: THE BILL's BILLED numeral begins its count-up (skipped entirely on the CLEAN state, which shows the word CLEAN with no count); its settle-voice fires at t=360+22*34=1108ms
t=560ms / t=620ms: the CREDITED and BILLED receipts (`.rl-receipt`) pop their rows in, staggered 90ms apart per row, via `kp-slot-anim`
t=700ms + k*26ms: the strain-left meter's up-to-24 segments light one at a time
t=700ms: the RECOVERED cell's piece glyph slots in (`kp-slot-anim`); its flavour line begins typing at t=760ms
t=820ms + i*110ms: the draft cards (or the dry message) slot in
t=900ms + i*70ms: the pouch strip glyphs slot in
t=1500ms: the masthead verdict slab locks (`rl-slab-lock 200ms steps(4)`), and if a draft was offered, `unlock` fires at this same instant
loadChoreography.ambientExceptions: the CLIENT CAM's rolling scan band (`rl-camroll 5.5s steps(30) infinite`) and its REC pip blink (`kp-cursor-blink 1.1s steps(2) infinite`) loop forever, which reads as a departure from law 7's 'ambient chrome never moves' until you check loadout-eva: `.lo-mon .roll` and its REC pip carry the identical infinite loops. Both are read as the camera's own diegetic behaviour (a live monitor rolls; a recording light blinks), not as UI chrome, which is the same call the reference build already made and had accepted; not a new departure, so not flagged as a violation.

items.variationsNote: SCENARIO's default on load is ROUGH WIN (ticket 2 of 3), not the day's first ticket (CLEAN SWEEP, ticket 1 of 3); this mirrors dadlog's own 'default to the most representative state, not the first one' convention and is a fine call, noted only for completeness.
acceptance: THE BILL's three cells are the largest text/glyphs on the page in every scenario and viewport; the masthead verdict slab is visibly smaller and never approaches the bill numerals' scale

in the DAY 8 STRAINED scenario only, the BILLED cell's numeral floods inverse video, the risk-flash plate blinks on a 1.2s steps(2) cadence, and the strain-left meter shows fewer than 9 of 24 segments lit (18/100 rounds to 4); the CREDITED cell and the RECOVERED cell never take on any of these three signals in this or any other scenario

the capped-bill inverse receipt row ('strain billed, capped / -40 max'), the LEFT ON THE BENCH status pill, the lost pouch slot, and the trap-round tick marks on the ECG trace render in the hazard tone, visibly distinct from the risk-band tone used on the BILLED cell in the same scenario
CLEAN SWEEP's BILLED cell shows the literal word CLEAN in the nominal tone in place of a numeral, with no count-up and no receipt rows

the AUGMENT CACHE shows all four states on demand: PICK ONE (ROUGH WIN, CLEAN SWEEP), INSTALLED (after picking, with the reticle-cornered card and its INSTALLED stamp), DRY (CAP AND DRY, a dashed message, no cards), and the EJECT swap panel (DAY 8 STRAINED, clicking either offered boost card), with the EJECT panel replacing the draft cards in the same DOM slot rather than adding a row
the four telemetry values render only as unboxed gutter ticks; no boxed sparkline graph appears anywhere on the page
the dive log shows at most 8 lines, laid out in 2 columns, directly beneath the strain trace it annotates

all three supported viewports (16:9 900px window, 21:9 980px window, 1280x800 laptop 790px window) render the identical arrangement: gutter beside bill and trace, cache full width beneath, no tab strip

no internal scrollbar appears on `.term-body` at any SCENARIO x VIEWPORT combination; total window height is measured against the 820px ceiling via the law-10 CDP harness (I did not run it myself this pass; see flaggedConcerns for why the ratio check below needs the same harness)
no `border-radius` appears anywhere except the CRT tube (`.lo-stage.crt-on`, `.lo-glass`, `.lo-stage.crt-on .lo-glass`)
no em dash or en dash appears anywhere in rendered text
both SCHEME options (NERV, TOKYO NIGHT) resolve all eight roles to visibly distinct values, and CRT OFF removes all six glass layers outright rather than fading them

switching FEED changes only the CLIENT CAM cell (tint presence, image source, grayscale filter); the print stays at 1:1 native pixels (162x234 in the >800px WIDE range, 162x186 cropped at the 700-800px tight end) and is never resampled

under prefers-reduced-motion, the entire page renders its fully-settled state (both numerals or CLEAN, the drawn trace, all 8 log lines, all cards/ticks/pouch slots, the locked slab) in one frame with no visible count-up, typewriter, slot-in, or scan-wipe, while `ledgerLock` and `unlock` (see flaggedConcerns on naming) still fire at their normal relative instants

flaggedConcerns.concern: computed focal-to-second-largest ratio falls short of law 2's stated 2.2x benchmark
flaggedConcerns.detail: Working the actual clamp() values against the actual grid math (not measured live; I have no CDP/Bash access this session) at 16:9 (900px term): the bill row's content column is ~669px, so a CREDITED/BILLED cell is ~207px wide after the 1fr/1fr/1.15fr split, and `clamp(44px,26cqi,78px)` resolves to ~54px there, not the 78px ceiling. The masthead slab's `clamp(22px,3.4cqi,32px)` resolves against the full ~870px content width (it is not inside its own container), landing at its 32px ceiling. Ratio: ~54/32 = 1.7x. At 21:9 (980px term) I get ~60/32 = 1.9x. At the laptop's tight-end breakpoint (790px term, narrower gutter and cell padding) I get ~46/26 = 1.8x. All three clear the law's explicit FAILURE case ('1.3x... has no hierarchy') with real margin, but all three fall short of the reference build's own achieved 2.2x. Recommend shrinking `--rl-fs-slab`'s ceiling (e.g. to ~26px) rather than growing the bill numeral further into its already-narrow third-of-a-row cell: the demo's own argument is that the verdict is DELIBERATELY subordinate, so a smaller slab both closes the ratio gap and reinforces the argument being made. Flagging with the arithmetic shown rather than asserting a fix, since I have not measured the live page; recommend a CDP pass before sign-off.
flaggedConcerns.severity: worth fixing before approval, not a hard blocker

flaggedConcerns.concern: DAY 8 STRAINED scenario's tier/day math does not reconcile with Bram Hollander's real customer data
flaggedConcerns.detail: The scenario computes CREDITED as `40 + 25*5 = 165` (tier 5) per its own code comment, and labels the ticket DAY 08. But `content/customers.ts` gives Bram Hollander `tiers: [2, 3]` (id `bram-hollander`), and `content/arc.ts`'s day 8 config caps `jobTiers` at `[4, 4, 4]` (no day offers tier 5 until day 9, and even then only as the last slot). No real generation could produce a tier-5 Bram Hollander ticket, on day 8 or any day. The win line and figure art are correctly verbatim (`bram-hollander`'s own shipped `winLine` and device), so nothing here invents fiction; it is a transcription slip in the numbers only. Recommend either dropping to a tier Bram's data supports (tier 3: `40+25*3=115`, still leaves room for the 40-cap chip bill to read as a close call) or, if the higher pay is wanted for scenario variety, swapping to a customer whose `tiers` actually reach 5.
flaggedConcerns.severity: should fix before this graduates past a study; copy/art are fine, only the derived numbers are wrong

flaggedConcerns.concern: the 'no piece this ticket' empty branch is neither exercised by a scenario nor defensively handled in code
flaggedConcerns.detail: report.tsx's own poster logic has three branches: cleanRun banked, patchDrop (banked or capped), and a genuine null/null case rendering 'NO PIECE THIS TICKET' with the pointer line 'Nothing came off this one. The next clean run still banks.' (verbatim shipped copy). All four built SCENARIOS objects always populate `S.piece` with a head/mask/status; `buildBill()`'s piece-cell code unconditionally reads `S.piece.head` and only guards `S.piece.mask !== null` for the glyph itself, so setting `S.piece = null` would throw rather than render the empty branch. This is one of the five empty branches the brief explicitly names under law 4 ('a dry cache, no piece this ticket, a full pouch, a zero chip, an empty payout receipt'); of the five, only this one is currently unreachable. Recommend making the piece-cell builder defensive against `S.piece === null` (rendering the verbatim NO PIECE THIS TICKET / pointer-line pair inside the same fixed-footprint cell) even if no SCENARIO button is added to demonstrate it live this cycle.
flaggedConcerns.severity: should fix before sign-off; low effort, the fallback copy already exists verbatim in report.tsx

flaggedConcerns.concern: `ledgerLock` duplicates the loadout-eva cycle's pending `instrumentLock` preset
flaggedConcerns.detail: The demo's inline `SFX.ledgerLock` is `{type:'square', freq:392, dur:0.075, vol:0.11, lpf:1800}` -- identical, parameter for parameter, to loadout-eva's `SFX.instrumentLock` in the same file family, and to the `instrumentLock` sfxr item already sitting in pipeline/proposals/ux-agent.json awaiting integration (same character: 'quieter and lower-pitched than tick, so several in a row read as a settle'). Both surfaces use it for the identical moment (a hero numeral's count-up landing). I recommend NOT proposing a second sfxr preset under a second name for the same sound; the Orchestrator should rename this demo's `ledgerLock` calls to `instrumentLock` at integration, so REPAIR.LOG and LOADOUT.CFG share one preset in audio.ts rather than two that could drift apart under future tuning. No new sfx item is filed in this SPEC.json for that reason.
flaggedConcerns.severity: integration-time cleanup, not a review blocker

flaggedConcerns.detail: index.html's own top-of-file role table (lines ~38-40) says note owns 'the // prefixes' broadly; in the actual CSS this is true of the eyebrow/units/tick-labels/nouns/kind-tags but NOT of the bill cells' own `// CREDITED` / `// BILLED` / `// [piece head]` name labels (`.rl-cname`), which correctly stay on plain `--ch` to match loadout-eva's `.lo-pname` precedent. The CSS is right; only the comment overclaims. Worth a one-line tightening at integration, not a functional change.
